[SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781) supports causal attention with residual connections and normalization; [ReZero](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v161/bachlechner21a/bachlechner21a.pdf) provides evidence for zero-initialized scalar residual gates. Practical adaptation, rather than a directly established recommendation result: add a history branch as h′=h+g·r, initialize g near zero, and explicitly bound the branch norm relative to h. Normalization alone does not guarantee this bound when scales are learned. Pool only nonpadding positions at or before each training timestep; clamp top-k to the valid prefix length, renormalize selected weights, and return zero for empty histories. These safeguards prevent future leakage and short-sequence numerical failures.

For validation uncertainty, retain paired per-user hit indicators for baseline and candidate on identical users and candidates. Resample user pairs independently within each category, then compute the equal-weight mean of four category HR@10 differences; report a 95% bootstrap interval. [SciPy’s bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html) supports shared-index paired resampling. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. This interval conditions on the fixed candidate draws; it does not measure training-seed or negative-sampling variability.

Keep the pinned sampled HR@10 as the selection objective. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings, so sampled gains cannot establish full-catalog gains. Repeated checkpoint and hyperparameter selection can also overfit validation noise; ordinary paired intervals do not correct that adaptive selection bias ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume11/cawley10a/cawley10a.pdf)).
